title: Malaysia May Let Creators Stop AI From Scraping Their Work Under Proposed Copyright Changes
key_facts: MyIPO director-general Yusnieza Syarmila Yusoff spoke at a media forum on 6 Oct 2026, according to SAYS citing The Edge Malaysia.
The government is evaluating an opt-out mechanism so rights holders can refuse unauthorised data mining of their works.
She named two issues: how training data is used, and who owns AI-generated output.
MyIPO is holding sessions with industry to set limits on the types, purposes and volume of content used for data mining.
She said laws should not be so restrictive as to stifle trade, investment and technology growth.
The review is still under discussion; no amendment is final.
quote_evidence: "We are exploring the possibility of introducing provisions related to data mining that also give rights holders the choice to opt out, namely, not allowing their works to be used," Yusnieza said.
The ongoing review remains under active discussion with various stakeholders before any official legislative amendments are finalised.
why_it_matters_hint: Malaysia is considering an opt-out right for creators against AI training, which would be a choice for rights holders, not a ban.
notes: SAYS cites The Edge Malaysia for the quote.
